resources.string: Lets computers you pair in PhoneAPI read the screen and send input.

PhoneAPI lets computers you pair over your local network, such as scripts, API clients, and AI agents, read this phone\'s screen and tap, swipe, and type on it. It needs the accessibility service because that is the only way Android lets an app see and operate other apps. Nothing is sent to a cloud service. Only computers you approve in the PhoneAPI app can connect, and you can revoke them there at any time.

PhoneAPI lets a computer you pair, such as a script, an API client, or an AI agent using MCP, see this phone\'s screen and control it over your local network. Everything runs on this phone; nothing goes through a cloud service.
Server: not listening. Connect to Wi-Fi or Ethernet.

Android only lets an app read other apps\' screens and tap on them through its accessibility service. Android will warn that PhoneAPI can see everything on screen and act for you: that is what a paired computer uses it for. Only computers you approve below can connect.
Accessibility service: off. Open the settings, find PhoneAPI (under Installed or Downloaded apps), and turn it on.
If Android says the setting is restricted, open App info, tap the ⋮ menu, choose Allow restricted settings, then try again. Android does this for apps installed outside an app store.

Put the computer on the same Wi-Fi as this phone, tap Pair a computer, and open the address shown in a browser on the computer. The browser will warn that the connection is not private because the phone uses its own certificate; choose Advanced, then continue. Enter a name for the computer and tap Allow here. The page then shows the address and token to give your API client or AI agent.
Connect this phone to Wi-Fi or Ethernet to pair. PhoneAPI only listens on the local network.
Open this address on the computer. Pairing closes in %1$d:%2$02d, or when you leave this screen.
Using ADB? With the phone connected over USB, this command prints the same details without a browser:
\"%1$s\" at %2$s will be able to see this phone\'s screen and control it until you revoke it.

Without the helper, a paired computer can read the screen, tap, swipe, type, and launch apps. The helper adds faster injected input, screen and audio streaming, Chrome control, and force-stopping apps. Android only allows that from developer tools, so start it once in one of these ways. On Android 11 and later, PhoneAPI restarts it by itself after that.
